name: Estate jobs end to end: getting items and approvals to the executor or trust officer
summary: The estate road from named lines to written approval and items leaving is well built for the Transition Concierge (TC) on the happy path. Send request is one press. It makes a dated filed copy and a Gmail draft with the PDF to both fiduciaries, copies counsel, writes the letter in the matter's words (Successor Trustee and "the trust's records" on a trust; "Personal Representative or Successor Trustee" on Both), handles partial signatures and ratification, and flags a draft that changed. A full approval round with two signers took 11 TC presses (e2). Sign-out on the iPad files a PDF and marks each line gone. Most of the risk sits behind that happy path, in what the paper proves and what the discerning reader receives. Two defects need fixing now. First, a recorded approval is not tied to what it approved: a painting approved for auction at Kodner can be retyped to go to a beneficiary, or a flatware set to an estate buyer, or its value raised tenfold. The approval stays complete, the iPad offers the sign-out, and the Disposition Ledger prints "Authorized by Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth" against a destination neither ever saw. Second, a firearm set to Donate or Junk (one bulk press does it) reads "Cleared to carry … takes it to Goodwill Palm Beach", and the signed request names Goodwill as the licensed dealer. Beyond those, the trust attorney or bank trust officer gets a Court Inventory stamped FINAL, with an adoption block, over 24 Agent Two figures nobody reviewed. The request the fiduciaries sign carries unreviewed names and values with no stamp. The photographs depend on this device's 2 MB thumbnail cache (124 of 300 on a full house; the PDF then tells counsel to "re-open this tab"). No paper carries a per-item photo link, a comparable or a reviewer. The package never shows counsel the signed papers. When a fiduciary strikes a line, nothing records it: the line comes back unchanged on the next request. Several close-out records count one signature or one same-day copy as everyone's. To make a 40-line, two-fiduciary approval a single round: pin each approval to the line's destination, recipient and value; record a strike as a decline with a new direction; add the planned DocuSign route with group initials and per-line approve or strike; and let the paper link every photograph and its valuation support.
works_well: Send request (sendApprovalRequest) is one press from the Releases card. It reads the sheet, files a DATED copy, builds the PDF and makes a Gmail draft to every fiduciary with counsel and agreements@ copied, and the notice says exactly what went (e1/e2: To t.ashworth@ and nora@, Cc ann@lowe.law; uploads show the dated filename).

The request reads as a letter in the matter's words. On a trust: 'Daniel Price, Successor Trustee / Ruth Price, Co-Trustee … filed with the trust's records'. On Both: 'Personal Representative or Successor Trustee' and 'the estate and trust records'. On contested probate: the court derived from the case number (e4, e7).

Partial approval is handled honestly. Recording Thomas alone saves, the dialog's note says 'Nora Ashworth has not signed yet: these lines stay on the next request', and the second recording names exactly which line each signer still owes (e2).
Grouped initials keep the paper light: on a 52-line trust request, 2 group-initial rows, 8 own-initial boxes for lines of $500 or more, and one initial for the firearms batch (e4).
Ratification of a line that left before every signature prints apart, names who still signs and says nothing is undone (e6: 'Already released: for ratification … for the signature of Nora Ashworth').
A waiting draft that changed is flagged, never refused, and Discard draft keeps the history and offers Send request again (e11).

Sign-out on the glass: only approved lines are offered, the pad refuses a tap, the PDF is filed to Signed Records and the lines read as gone (e6: pickup:Kodner Galleries:e01,e02; invRecordedGone true).

The staff rule refuses at the row with a plain sentence and puts the box back (e6: 'Anthony Graziano Jr is with Havellin, so #10 Walnut dresser cannot be sold or released to them. Nothing was changed.').

The package refuses before activation and asks before sending an unfinished inventory, naming the gaps (e9: '4 rooms not yet locked, 2 lines with no disposition and 2 lines with no value … Send it anyway?'), and it shares both photo folders with counsel and the fiduciaries.
measurements: One approval round, Ashworth, 3 lines, two co-representatives recorded on separate returns, one signed copy filed: 11 TC presses (open Releases, Send request, I've sent it, Record the signed request, untick 1, tick signer, Record approval, file copy, then Record the signed request, tick, Record approval, Done). Script EST/e2.js, out/e2.out 'PRESSES 11'.

Trust estate full house, 48 shots: naming, room check and Agent Two ran by themselves in 3.3 s against the stub (actions agentIdentify x3, agentRoomCheck, agentValue x3). The request then carried 52 lines with 2 group-initial rows, 8 own boxes and 1 firearms initial, and 0 photographs (no thumbnails cached). EST/e4.js, out/e4.out.

Thumbnail cache at 300 lines with 16 KB thumbnails: 124 kept (1,988,093 chars, under the 2,000,000 cap). The Estate Inventory Report printed 124 and the sentence '176 items have no photograph available on this device … re-open this tab with a connection to include them'. EST/e10.js, out/e10.out.

Drive links per line in the PDFs counsel or fiduciaries receive: 0 in the Estate Inventory Report, the Trust Schedule, the Disposition Ledger, the Release Approval Request and the Court Inventory (grep of the saved HTML under EST/out/: e4-eir-trust.html, e4-trust-trust.html, e4-ledger-trust.html, e1-request.html, e8-court-after-remove.html).

Court Inventory status, probate, 24 lines valued by Agent Two and 0 reviewed: 'FINAL 24 values not yet reviewed … Reviewed and adopted by: ____ Daniel Price · Personal Representative'. EST/e8.js, out/e8.out.
Removing the 'nothing to list' lines so the Court Inventory can go FINAL: 2 presses plus 1 confirm per line (2 lines on 24 shots; one in twelve on the stub's catalogue). EST/e8.js.

Approval surviving an edit: e01 approved Oct 12 for Auction to Kodner, retyped to Distribute to Margaret Ashworth: complete=true, sign-out kind 'receipt'. Its value typed from $2,400 to $24,000: complete=true, needsAppr=true, 'Sign out 2 to Kodner Galleries' still offered. EST/e3.js and e11.js.
verifier_note: The EST report holds up well. Both fix-now defects reproduced independently through the real row controls (EST-01, EST-02). EST-01 is worse than reported: once a request has been sent, a retyped recipient is recorded as approved against the new destination, while the paper carried the old one. Two descriptions overstate today's behaviour. EST-09: the 'nothing to list' cleanup takes 3 presses plus a confirm (Unnamed shots chip, Select all, Remove lines), not presses per line. EST-17: a Junk line can be marked gone through its per-line Date of Disposition (there is no bulk route and no sign-out). EST-03 reproduces, but it is Anthony's recorded decision (AGENT_TWO_SPEC §12.2, 2026-10-06), so it is DECIDED_CONFLICT. EST-19 is the DocuSign request already listed under Open work. EST-20 is the mirror of the known 'Court Inventory offered on a trust-only desk, by design'. I lowered EST-07 to medium; the other severities stand. My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/EST-verify/ (v1 to v4), with their output in out/.

findings.title: A written approval is not tied to what it approved: changing destination, recipient or value keeps the line approved and offered for sign-out
findings.where: Desk row 'Where it goes' / 'Who takes it' / Total; Releases card sign-out rows; Disposition Ledger 'Authorized by'. invApprovalComplete (havellin.html:31383) reads only authBy and approvalDate; _invEdit (29700) and _invBulkApply (37298) never touch authBy when disposition, channel or fmv change; approvalRequestChanged (32647) compares only a WAITING draft (docDraftPending) and nothing compares after I've sent it; invRecordRequestApproval and invRecordApproval (33187, 33094) list each line as it reads now, not as the paper read.
findings.evidence: EST/e3.js (out/e3.out): e01 'Harbor scene oil painting', approved Oct 12 by both fiduciaries for Auction to Kodner Galleries, changed on its row to Distribute and Margaret Ashworth: {complete:true, kind:'receipt'}. The Releases card then offered 'Sign out 1 to Margaret Ashworth' and 'Print receipt', and the ledger printed '1 Harbor scene oil painting Distribute Margaret Ashworth Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12, 2026)'. e02, approved for Auction to Kodner, changed to Sell to Palm Beach Estate Buyers: still complete, 'Sign out 1 to Palm Beach Estate Buyers' offered. EST/e11.js: e01's Total typed $24,000: complete:true and needsAppr:true, still in 'Sign out 2 to Kodner Galleries', and no 'not yet appraised' caution ever goes before the fiduciaries. By code: a line whose recipient changes after the request is sent and before it is signed is recorded against its new destination by Record the signed request.
findings.tc_impact: The TC is never told that an approval no longer covers the line. A correction made in good faith (a better buyer, the right beneficiary, the appraisal landing) turns into a release with no authority behind it. The trust attorney reading the ledger sees both fiduciaries 'authorizing' a $2,400 painting going to a daughter, or a $24,000 item going to an estate buyer, which neither ever approved. That is the failure the written-release rule exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: Record what each signature approved. invSaveApproval stamps on every line `authFor` = disposition|trimmed recipient|value band (reuse approvalRequestSig's fields, one short string per line; approvalRequestSig itself fingerprints a whole request). invApprovalComplete also asks that the line still matches `authFor`. Otherwise it reads 'approval was for an earlier destination' (a caution on the row, the bar and the request, which prints 'previously approved for Auction · Kodner Galleries'), drops out of sign-out, and goes back on the next request. The value band: re-ask when a value crosses INV_LINE_INITIAL_MIN or invAppraisalThreshold, or rises by more than a set percentage (Anthony to set it). Extend approvalRequestChanged past the draft: after I've sent it, compare each line with req.sig. The Record dialog then shows any line changed since the paper went, unticked, with 'changed after this request went: ask again'. Flag, never refuse, except that a stale approval never counts as authority.
findings.vnote: Reproduced on step99's Ashworth estate through the row's own select and Who-takes-it box. e01 was approved by both fiduciaries on Oct 12 for Auction to Kodner. After changing it to Distribute and Margaret Ashworth: complete=true, kind=receipt, the Releases card offers 'Sign out 1 to Margaret Ashworth', and the ledger prints '1 Harbor scene oil painting Distribute Margaret Ashworth Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth (Oct 12, 2026)'. e02's Total typed up to $18,000: still complete, needsAppr=true, 'Sign out 1 to Kodner Galleries' still offered. New in v2: after Send request and I've sent it, e04's recipient was retyped from Goodwill to 'Salvation Army Thrift'. approvalRequestChanged returned [] (it only reads a pending draft, havellin.html:32649). The Record dialog listed '#4 … Donate · Salvation Army Thrift', and saving made e04 complete against a recipient the signed paper never carried. No notice at any step.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v1.js -> out/v1.out (lines 'EST-01 after e01', 'after e02 total $18,000', LEDGER #1); EST-verify/v2.js -> out/v2.out ('approvalRequestChanged after I've sent it = []', 'DIALOG 1', 'e04 … complete:true'); code havellin.html:31383 invApprovalComplete, 29700-29790 _invEdit never touches authBy

findings.title: A firearm set to Donate or Junk is 'Cleared to carry' to the charity or hauler, and the signed request names it as the licensed dealer
findings.where: Bulk bar 'Set disposition…' and 'Set recipient'; the row's 'Where it goes' (every disposition offered on a Firearms line); line record 'Firearm' block (_invFirearmPanelHtml 39984); Release Approval Request 'Firearms: written authority' (32523). invTransportDealer (30034) returns the channel for any disposition but Distribute; invTransportBlocked (30006) is satisfied by any channel.
findings.evidence: EST/e4.js: 'Select all' then 'Set disposition… Donate' and 'Set recipient Goodwill Palm Beach' on a trust house caught 4 Remington shotguns. There was no flag ('✓ Donate set on 52 items'), and the request printed 'Your initial below … is your written authority for Havellin's named principal to transport each non-NFA firearm listed here, by the serial and to the licensed dealer printed against it … 11 Remington 870 pump shotgun not recorded Goodwill Palm Beach'. EST/e5.js and e6.js, with a serial and both approvals recorded: g1 Donate→Goodwill blocked="" dealer=Goodwill Palm Beach; g2 Junk→Haul-It Junk Removal blocked=""; the record reads '✓ Cleared to carry. Havellin's named principal alone takes it to Goodwill Palm Beach, in a locked case.'
findings.tc_impact: The firearms protocol says every firearm goes to a licensed dealer. One bulk press across a closet lets the app tell the TC, and the fiduciaries on the paper they initial, that a donation charity or a junk hauler is the dealer, and then clears the transport. This is the one area where the app refuses rather than flags, and here it does neither.
findings.proposal: A firearm's dealer is never read from a free-text channel. invTransportDealer answers only from a recorded dealer: invDealerRoute, or a channel matching a Vendor Directory row in a licensed-dealer category (add an 'FFL / Licensed Firearms Dealer' category). Otherwise 'dealer not named'. On a Firearms line, offer and accept only Auction, Consign or Sell (to a dealer), Distribute (through a dealer), Hold and Keep. Refuse Donate and Junk in _invEdit and _invBulkApply, as the staff rule does: by name, nothing written. The bulk apply skips firearms and says '4 firearms left as they were: a firearm goes to a licensed dealer'. The request's firearms block prints 'licensed dealer not named yet' for any channel that is not a dealer.
findings.vnote: Added an Agent-One-named 'Remington 870 pump shotgun' (Firearms) to Ashworth. Through the row select it was set to Donate (offered: Auction, Consign, Distribute, Donate, Hold, Junk, Keep, Sell) with the recipient Goodwill Palm Beach, and nothing objected. The request printed 'Serial not recorded · to Goodwill Palm Beach, a licensed dealer' and 'Every one goes to a licensed dealer'. I then typed a serial in the record and recorded both signatures through the bulk bar's Record approval dialog. invTransportBlocked returned '' and the record read '✓ Cleared to carry. Havellin's named principal alone takes it to Goodwill Palm Beach, in a locked case.' invTransportDealer (30034) returns any channel off Distribute. firearms-protocol.html:581 says firearms are 'dispositioned through a licensed dealer'.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v1.js -> out/v1.out ('EST-02 g1 after Donate', 'EST-02 request firearms block', 'EST-02 g1 after serial+approval', 'EST-02 record firearm block'); out/v1-request.html

findings.title: The Court Inventory and Trust Schedule go FINAL, with an adoption block, over Agent Two figures nobody has reviewed
findings.where: More ▾ Court Inventory / Trust Schedule, and the package. printCourtInventory status (havellin.html:34113) and printTrustSchedule (34266): _draftWhy never counts unreviewed values; _avUnreviewedStamp (39328) only prints a badge beside FINAL.
findings.evidence: EST/e8.js (out/e8.out), probate, 24 lines named and valued by the agents, 0 reviewed: 'FINAL 24 values not yet reviewed … Values are estimated fair market value as of date of death. Reviewed and adopted by: ____ Daniel Price · Personal Representative'. Every basis reads 'general estimate', including 'Oil on canvas harbor scene … signed lower right (illegible)' at $1,200.
findings.tc_impact: A personal representative adopts a §733.604 inventory that is verified under oath, and counsel files it. A FINAL beside '24 values not yet reviewed' invites signing a schedule of machine figures no Havellin person has looked at. A Palm Beach estate attorney will read that as unreliable work, and 'who stands behind this value' has no answer.
findings.proposal: Keep the paper printable at any stage, but tie the status and the adoption or receipt block to the one look. While agentValueUnreviewed holds on any scheduled line, the status reads 'DRAFT — N values not yet reviewed by Havellin' and the block is withheld, as for an unvalued line. The work bar's Unsure and Not reviewed chips are the way through, and Mark reviewed across a selection clears them. The package confirm (probatePackageGaps) names unreviewed values too.
findings.decided_conflict: Domain rules, Inventory: 'Review gates nothing; documents in progress are stamped IN PROGRESS and never withheld.' The document is still not withheld; only FINAL and the signature block wait, as they already do for an unvalued line.
findings.vnote: The observation reproduces. On a 24-shot probate house the real pipeline ran by itself (agentIdentify x2, agentRoomCheck, agentValue x2) and left 0 of 26 lines reviewed. After the two empty lines were removed, the Court Inventory read 'FINAL 24 values not yet reviewed' with the 'Reviewed and adopted by … Daniel Price · Personal Representative / authorized fiduciary' block. This is Anthony's answer in AGENT_TWO_SPEC §12.2 (2026-10-06): 'An unreviewed agent value counts as valued for FINAL; the schedule says N values not yet reviewed … and nothing is withheld'. CLAUDE.md Domain rules (Agent Two's figures) say the same: 'An unreviewed agent figure counts as valued … print _avUnreviewedStamp beside their status'. The code comment at 34149 says 'never holding it back (P23)'. The auditor cited 'Review gates nothing' but missed this, the more direct rule. Worth putting back to Anthony as a question, since a PR adopts this paper under oath, but it is not a defect.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v4.js -> out/v4.out ('Court status (after cleanup): … FINAL 24 values not yet reviewed', 'adoption block'); out/v4-court-after.html; AGENT_TWO_SPEC.md:295-297

findings.title: The Release Approval Request carries unreviewed agent names and values with no stamp
findings.where: printApprovalRequest (havellin.html:32310): it calls neither _invProgressStamp nor _avUnreviewedStamp (those are read at 30990, 31141, 31143, 34150, 34283, 34540, 35632); the send's notice (sendApprovalRequest 32792).
findings.evidence: EST/e1.js: the request Ashworth's fiduciaries receive lists '10 Walnut dresser … $450 Sell Palm Beach Estate Buyers' (namedBy agent, reviewed 0) with no mark. EST/e4.js: the trust request carried 52 lines whose 48 values the Trust Schedule stamps '48 values not yet reviewed'; the request says nothing, and the Estate Inventory Report and ledger stamp 'IN PROGRESS — 0 of 52 items reviewed'. The work bar says 'Client documents print with an IN PROGRESS stamp until every line is ticked'.
findings.tc_impact: The paper the fiduciaries sign is the one paper that releases property, and it is the only inventory paper without the review stamp. A trustee approving 'Sell for est. $450' does not know that no person checked what the thing is or what it is worth.
findings.proposal: Print _avUnreviewedStamp, plus a per-line 'value not yet reviewed' badge, on the request, and stamp 'names or values on N lines not yet reviewed'. The send's notice says so in amber and offers 'Mark reviewed' on those lines first. Flag, never refuse.
findings.vnote: printApprovalRequest (havellin.html:32310-32646) calls neither _invProgressStamp nor _avUnreviewedStamp; grep lists their only callers as 30990, 31141, 31143, 34150, 34283, 34540 and 35632. Ashworth's request printed the agent-named, unreviewed '#10 Walnut dresser … $450 Sell Palm Beach Estate Buyers' with IN PROGRESS=false and 'not yet reviewed'=false. The same claim is false in the guides: evening-desk-guide.html:452 says 'Papers print marked IN PROGRESS until every item is reviewed', and the playbook (concierge-guide.html:916) says the same of client documents, yet the one paper that releases property carries no such mark.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v1.js -> out/v1.out ('EST-04 request stamps: IN PROGRESS false not yet reviewed false'); out/v1-request.html

findings.title: A line a fiduciary strikes is not recorded: it returns unchanged on the next request, and the other signer's approval stands
findings.where: Record a signed approval dialog (invRecordApproval 33094, INV_REQ_UNTICK_TXT 'Untick any line the signed copy struck out'); invSaveApproval (33218); approvalRequestState and the next request; evening-desk-guide.html ('Untick any the signed copy struck out').
findings.evidence: EST/e2.js: Thomas struck #10 Walnut dresser (unticked) and Nora signed all three. Afterwards #10 reads 'awaiting written approval' and '#10 goes back on the next approval request', with Nora's approval kept: authBy 'Nora Ashworth'. Nothing records that Thomas declined it, the next request asks him again for the same sale to the same buyer, and the guide says nothing about what to do next.
findings.tc_impact: The fiduciary's instruction is lost and must live in the TC's memory or email. The next round re-asks for something already refused: an extra round trip of days, and with a trust officer an unprofessional one. The co-fiduciary's lone approval of a refused sale stays on the record.
findings.proposal: In Record the signed request, an unticked line opens two choices: 'struck by …' (tick the fiduciary) and 'their direction' (Hold, Keep, a new disposition and recipient, or a note). Save records `declinedBy`/`declinedOn`/`declineNote` and moves the line to Hold, or to the new direction (EST-01 then marks any partial approval stale). The line stays off requests until a person sets a new destination. The ledger and the package record print 'declined by Thomas Ashworth, Oct 26'. Update the desk guide.
findings.vnote: Driven on Ashworth. Send request, then I've sent it, then Record the signed request: unticked #10 Walnut dresser and ticked Thomas only. Then a second Record for Nora, ticking all lines. Afterwards e10 has authBy 'Nora Ashworth' and complete=false, and no decline, strike or refusal key exists on the line. approvalRequestState.open=['e10'], and the next request prints '10 Walnut dresser … $450 Sell Palm Beach Estate Buyers Signed so far by Nora Ashworth (Oct 26, 2026); still to sign: Thomas Ashworth', asking him again for the same sale. The guides say only 'Untick any the signed copy struck out' (evening-desk-guide.html:579, concierge-guide.html:1020) and say nothing about what follows. The proposal fits the domain rules: partial approvals stay recorded, never refused (Q24).
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v2.js -> out/v2.out ('e10 {…authBy:"Nora Ashworth"…keys:[]}', 'EST-05 next request #10 row')

findings.title: Photographs on the papers come from a capped device cache (124 of 300); no paper links an item to its photograph, yet the papers say they are 'reference-numbered'
findings.where: _invPrintThumb (havellin.html:30687) reads only this device's cache; INV_THUMB_CACHE_MAX 2,000,000 (28521) evicts the oldest, and _invThumbTried (28566-28600) never refetches in the session. Estate Inventory Report footer (31163); Court Inventory, Trust Schedule and Disposition Ledger print no photograph; Drive filenames are room+seq (40674), not item numbers.
findings.evidence: EST/e10.js: a 300-line estate with 16 KB thumbnails keeps 124. The Estate Inventory Report prints 124 images and '176 items have no photograph available on this device. The photographs are filed in the estate's Drive folder; re-open this tab with a connection to include them' (this page goes into the package PDF). EST/e1.js: the request's Photo column printed '📦 4', '🏺 7', '🪑 10' (category glyphs). Every saved PDF HTML holds 0 Drive file links, against the footer's claim 'Photographs are reference-numbered to the line items above'.
findings.tc_impact: The trust officer or executor cannot see what they are approving or adopting. Emoji in a Photo column look broken, and 'on this device / re-open this tab' are words meant for the TC, landing in counsel's inbox. In a shared folder of files named LivingRoom_INV_3, nothing maps item #23 to its photograph. The paper claims a reference-numbering the app never did (the CLAUDE.md rule 'never print a claim the app did not witness').
findings.proposal: Before any printer builds a page (print, view, send, package), fetch the thumbnails for that page's lines into a print-only map that ignores the cache cap (getThumbnails in batches), and fall back to a glyph only for a file Drive cannot serve, named as such. Make each line's Ref, or a small 'photo' link, its driveFileUrl on the Estate Inventory Report, Court Inventory, Trust Schedule, Contents List and request, and print it on the Court Inventory and Trust Schedule too. Drop the 'this device' sentence from client papers. The request's send shares the Estate Inventory photo folder with the fiduciaries, as the package does, so they can open each item before signing.
findings.vnote: 300-line probate house, with the getThumbnails stub answering every file at the size main-sync.gs calls real (~10 KB, 13,359 chars as a data URL). The in-memory cache kept 149 of 306 (1,991,982 chars, under INV_THUMB_CACHE_MAX 2,000,000), because _invSaveThumbCache deletes from the live object. The Estate Inventory Report printed 149 and told counsel '151 items have no photograph available on this device … re-open this tab with a connection to include them'. That remedy can never work: the cap evicts on every save, and _invThumbTried blocks a refetch in the session. The page has 0 Drive file links, yet it closes 'Photographs are reference-numbered to the line items above'. Real Drive filenames are hvlId_room_tag_seq_stamp.jpg (havellin.html:40675), not item numbers. v1 also showed category emoji printed in the request's Photo column.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v3.js -> out/v3.out ('cache {kept:149…}', 'EIR count 149 | sentence: 151 items…'); out/v3-eir.html; havellin.html:28521-28540, 30687, 31153-31163

findings.title: The estate package never shows counsel the signed papers: approvals, pickup lists, receipts and adopted schedules stay in an unshared folder
findings.where: Probate or Trust card, Send probate package: _pkgShareFolders (havellin.html:17982) shares Estate Inventory and As-Found only; probatePackageRecordHtml (17783) lists approvals 'as recorded' with no link; SIGNED_RECORDS_SUBFOLDER 'Signed Records' (25769) is never shared or linked.
findings.evidence: EST/e9.js: the email lists four PDFs, two photo folders and 'Release approvals and chain of custody', a Havellin-built table ('Who signed … as recorded from the signed approval returned to Havellin'). No signed request, pickup list, beneficiary receipt or donation receipt is attached or linked, and the shares went only to the AF and INV folders.
findings.tc_impact: The attorney is asked to take Havellin's word for every authority and every handover. The evidence exists in Drive, filed by the TC, but the reader cannot open it. A bank trust officer's file review will ask for exactly those signatures.
findings.proposal: In the package, share Signed Records with the addressee and copies too, or link each live signed record's fileUrl in the record page beside the approval act, receipt or pickup it proves (signedRecordsOf by kind, with signedBy and signedOn). Add a 'Signed papers' list to the email. The draft goes stale on a new filing, as probatePackageMovedSince already does for appraisal reports.
findings.vnote: By code. _pkgShareFolders (17982) resolves and shares only PHOTO_SUBFOLDER and AS_FOUND_SUBFOLDER. The email's drive() list (18104-18113) carries the pages, the appraisal reports (filed to Estate Inventory since Q93, so reachable), the two folders and the Havellin-built record. probatePackageRecordHtml (17783-17844) has 0 hrefs and says 'as recorded from the signed approval returned to Havellin'. Signed Records (approvals, pickups, receipts, donation receipts, adopted schedules) is never shared or linked. Lowered to medium: counsel can ask for the copies, and the record names every act.

findings.title: The valuation support (comparables, method, confidence, who reviewed) never reaches any paper
findings.where: Estate Inventory Report (printEstateInventoryReport 31014), Court Inventory, Trust Schedule. valComps is read only by the desk's _avPanelHtml (havellin.html:39280); valReviewedBy and valConf are printed nowhere.
findings.evidence: grep: valComps appears at 27542 (save list), 38611, 38646 and 39097 (writers) and 39280 (desk panel), and in no printer. EST/e4.js: the report's source column reads 'General estimate' / 'Auction comps' with the agent's basis sentence, and no comparable, date, link, reviewer or confidence.
findings.tc_impact: 'Every value defensible (its standard, date, method, evidence, who stands behind it)' fails on evidence and on who stands behind it. To answer an attorney's 'how did you get $1,800 for the flatware?' the TC has to open the desk and read it out. A twenty-year appraiser's spreadsheet at least names the comp.
findings.proposal: A 'Valuation Support' page, built from what the line already holds: for each researched or appraised line, and each line at or above $500, print the value, standard and date, method (research / going rate / appraisal / desk), up to three comparables (title, price, sale date, link), the WorthPoint search, the agent's confidence, and 'reviewed by <valReviewedBy or reviewedBy>, <date>' or 'appraised by <appraiser, credential>'. Offer it in More ▾, attach it in the package after the Estate Inventory Report, and name the reviewer in the report's source column.
findings.vnote: The stubbed Agent Two returned one comparable per line, with a title and a URL, and all 24 lines stored valComps. Neither the comparable's title nor its URL appears on the Court Inventory, the Estate Inventory Report or the Disposition Ledger, and none of them prints 'reviewed by' or a confidence. grep: valComps is read only at 27542 (save list), 38611/38646/39097 (writers) and 39280 (the desk panel); valReviewedBy and valConf are printed only on the desk (39263-39264). No decided rule keeps comparables off the papers.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v4.js -> out/v4.out ('EST-08 court/eir … comp title printed: false comp url printed: false reviewer: false confidence: false', 'withComps:24'); out/v4-eir.html, out/v4-court-after.html

findings.title: 'Nothing to list' lines stay inventory items on every paper and keep the Court Inventory in DRAFT until removed one by one
findings.where: Desk rows marked 'nothing to list' (havellin.html:39729, agentConf 'none'); every printer counts them; 'Select all' picks them.
findings.evidence: EST/e8.js: 'DRAFT — 2 items not yet valued … 1 item is recorded without a value …: #8 unnamed'. FINAL only after Remove line on each (2 presses plus a confirm per line). EST/e4.js: 'Select all' then Donate put '8 — · Dining Room 1 — Donate Goodwill Palm Beach' on the trustees' request, and the Estate Inventory Report counted 'Donate 52 items' for 48 things.
findings.tc_impact: Phantom items on the list the attorney receives, a schedule that never finalises for a reason the TC cannot see, and per-line cleanup on a drawer-heavy house.
findings.proposal: A line Agent One read as nothing to list is not an item. Exclude agentConf 'none' lines with no name from every printer, count and selection (Select all skips them), and offer one press on the work bar, 'Remove N empty photographs' (_invTombstoneLine with defer; photographs kept, Restore gives them back). Or tombstone the blank line automatically when the answer is empty, so the photograph stays in the record.
findings.vnote: Confirmed with a correction. On the 24-shot probate house, #8 and #20 came back 'nothing to list' and stayed inventory lines, and they held the Court Inventory at 'DRAFT — 2 items not yet valued'. Clearing them is not per line, though. The work bar's 'Unnamed shots 2' chip, then the group's Select all (filter-scoped, _invPickGroup 37219), then Remove lines took both off with one confirm, and the Court Inventory went FINAL. The real risk is a bulk Select all with no filter applied. The auditor's request shows it putting '📦 8 — · Dining Room 1 — Donate Goodwill Palm Beach' on the trustees' request (EST/out/e4-request-trust.html, made through the real Select all and bulk select). Excluding agentConf 'none' lines from papers and bulk picks is a sound fix.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v4.js -> out/v4.out ('none:["#8","#20"]', 'DRAFT — 2 items not yet valued', 'picked ["s7","s19"]', 'Remove 2 lines', 'after cleanup: … FINAL'); EST/out/e4-request-trust.html

findings.title: The desk cannot send the inventory itself to the fiduciary or counsel; there is only a print, and no package at all on Neither or an unanswered matter
findings.where: Work bar 'Estate Inventory PDF' (havellin.html:39408, print only); More ▾ papers print or view; the package lives on the dashboard's Probate or Trust card (probatePackageCardHtml 18196); estatePackageRoute is null on Neither or unanswered (e7 'PKG ROW: no package row').
findings.evidence: EST/e7.js: on 'unanswered' and 'neither' the desk offers Estate Inventory PDF / CSV / Approval Request and More ▾ prints, no send, and no package row on the dashboard. shareInventoryWithCounsel (36801) shares photo folders only. CLAUDE.md records 'documents go one at a time from the desk', but the only document the desk sends is the request.
findings.tc_impact: To give the representative an interim inventory before asking for approvals, the TC prints to PDF, attaches it by hand from another app, and nothing on the job records what went or to whom. The trust officer gets an unbranded attachment with no record of it.
findings.proposal: A 'Send' beside the Estate Inventory PDF (and in More ▾ for each schedule, the Contents List and the worklist) on sendApprovalRequest's path: sheet read, dated filed copy, PDF, Gmail draft to approvalRequestRecipients, docRecordSent under its own key, I've sent it on the work bar. Let the request's send attach the current Estate Inventory Report as the context the fiduciaries approve against.
findings.decided_conflict: Decided: 'An inventory package on a matter recorded Neither (Anthony, P18: documents go one at a time from the desk)'. This builds that one-at-a-time send and proposes no package.
findings.vnote: The work bar (havellin.html:39405-39420) offers the primary document as a print (Estate Inventory PDF, Contents List or Contents Record), a CSV and the Approval Request print. More ▾ papers print or open in the viewer. The only paper the desk sends is the release request. A one-at-a-time send from the desk fits the Decided item 'An inventory package on a matter recorded Neither (P18: documents go one at a time from the desk)' and proposes no package. It is a new feature under the feature freeze, so it belongs in the plan.
findings.vrepro: havellin.html:39405-39420 (_renderInvWorkbar), 39432-39439 (More ▾)

findings.title: The vendor pickup sheet is 'Signed by: Kodner Galleries' with no person's name, and promises a purpose column it does not print
findings.where: Sign out on the iPad dialog: ip-signer prefilled with the firm (openSignoutDialog, havellin.html:31803). signoutSheetHtml (31693): columns Item #, Description, Qty, Room, Condition, Approved in writing by.
findings.evidence: EST/e6.js (EST/out/e6-pickup-sheet.html): 'I received the items listed above … for the purpose recorded against each item … Signed by: Kodner Galleries, signed on the iPad'. The table has no disposition (Auction, Consign or Sell) and no value or photograph.
findings.tc_impact: A receipt signed by a company name is weak evidence of who took a $2,400 painting, and the acknowledgement points to a purpose the page never states. The bank trust officer would expect the individual's printed name 'for Kodner Galleries'.
findings.proposal: Start ip-signer blank for a vendor or charity (the blank-boxes rule). Require a person's name and print 'Signed by <name>, for <firm>'. Add a 'For' column (Auction / Consign / Sell / Donation) from the line's disposition, and a small photo thumbnail for identification (fetched as in EST-06).
findings.vnote: I opened 'Sign out 1 to Kodner Galleries' on Ashworth. #ip-signer was prefilled with 'Kodner Galleries' (openSignoutDialog 31803: signer.value = g.taker). The sheet built from it reads 'Signed by: Kodner Galleries, signed on the iPad', and its acknowledgement says 'for the purpose recorded against each item'. Its columns are Item #, Description, Qty, Room, Condition and 'Approved in writing by': no disposition, value or photograph. The header says only 'for sale or disposal as recorded against each item'. The box is editable, so a TC can type a person's name, but the default produces a company signature.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v2.js -> out/v2.out ('EST-11 signer prefill: "Kodner Galleries"', 'EST-11 sheet: …'); out/v2-kodner-sheet.html

findings.title: Same-day signatures merge into one act: the header overstates who approved, and an unfiled signer's paper goes unflagged
findings.where: Releases card 'Signed release approvals' (invApprovalBatches, havellin.html:31435, grouped by day); the Releases bar's unfiled count (deskFoldState 48207: a batch counts as filed if any copy is filed that day).
findings.evidence: EST/e2.js: Thomas (#4, #7) and Nora (#4, #7, #10) signed separate copies on the same day; only Thomas's was filed. The card reads 'Approved Oct 26, 2026 by Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth · 3 lines (#4, #7, #10) ⚠ Thomas Ashworth has not approved it … ✓ Signed release approval · signed by Thomas Ashworth'. The bar after Nora: '1 signed receipt owed · 1 on the request still unsigned · 3 ready to sign out', with no 'signed approval not filed'.
findings.tc_impact: Two fiduciaries returning scans on the same day is the common case. Nora's approval now has no paper behind it and nothing says so, and the act's header tells the attorney that Thomas approved #10.
findings.proposal: Key an act on day plus signer (or on the filed record's signedBy), list each signer's own lines under their name, and count 'not filed' per signer per day. Offer 'File the signed request' on the row for any signer with no copy.
findings.vnote: Driven: on the same day Thomas signed #4 and #7 and struck #10, while Nora signed all three. Only Thomas's copy was filed (its signedRecord names 'Thomas Ashworth'). invApprovalBatches gave one act: {date 2026-10-26, who 'Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth', lines [4,7,10], filed 1}. The card's header reads 'Approved Oct 26, 2026 by Thomas Ashworth; Nora Ashworth · 3 lines (#4, #7, #10)', followed by '⚠ Thomas Ashworth has not approved it … ✓ Signed release approval · signed by Thomas Ashworth'. The bar's bits had no 'not filed', because deskFoldState counts an act as filed when any copy of that day is (48207). Nora's signature has no paper on file and nothing says so, though the filed record's signedBy already shows it covers Thomas alone.
findings.vrepro: EST-verify/v2.js -> out/v2.out ('EST-12 batches', 'EST-12 card signed approvals', 'EST-12 deskFoldState bits')

findings.title: The Disposition Ledger's signed copy records no signer, so one signature passes for every fiduciary's
findings.where: Disposition Ledger card under Closing: signedCopyControlHtml(jid,'ledger',{ref, label}) with no signedBy (havellin.html:34703); ledgerDerivedLines (35089) is green on any copy; ledgerSigners (34413) prints a line per fiduciary. The adopted Court Inventory and Trust Schedule copies are the same.
findings.evidence: Code: the ledger prints a signature line for each of Thomas and Nora, but ledgerSignedCopies(job).length > 0 makes 'Disposition Ledger signed by the Personal Representative' ✓, and the card says 'the Personal Representative signs it' (EST/e12.js out). Release approvals, by contrast, require every fiduciary (invApprovalComplete).
findings.tc_impact: On a two-trustee estate the close-out sign-off can be one trustee's alone, and the record cannot say which. The same every-fiduciary rule the app enforces for releases is missing on the final record.
findings.proposal: The ledger and schedule File signed copy controls ask who signed (a tick per ledgerSigners or scheduleSigners, as Record approval does) and record signedBy. The derived line is green only once every fiduciary is on record, a partial one amber, naming who is missing. Card words: 'each representative signs it'.
findings.vnote: By code. _renderLedgerCard (34703) passes signedCopyControlHtml(jid,'ledger',{ref: LEDGER_SIGNED_REF, label}) with no signedBy. ledgerSignedCopies (34401) is any live copy. ledgerDerivedLines (35093-35094) is ok whenever sc.length > 0 and is labelled 'Disposition Ledger signed by the <approver>'. Yet the ledger prints a line for each ledgerSigners entry, and releases demand every fiduciary (invApprovalComplete). On a two-fiduciary estate one signature turns the close-out line green.

findings.title: Closing an estate does not name outstanding release paperwork (approvals, ratifications, receipts, donation receipts)
findings.where: Close job question: closeOpenWorkFlag (havellin.html:24595) names rooms not cleared, lines with no recipient and appraisal hand-offs only; jobCloseBlockers names vendors, keys and incidents.
findings.evidence: Code read of closeOpenWorkFlag: nothing about _invAwaitingApproval, invRatificationOwed, invReceiptOwed, donationReceiptLine or unfiled approvals, although the Releases bar computes each (e2: '1 signed receipt owed · 1 on the request still unsigned').
findings.tc_impact: A job can close with a $3,500 bequest released and no signed receipt, or a ratification never signed. Counsel finds it later, when the package or ledger arrives.
findings.proposal: Add to closeOpenWorkFlag (a flag, never a refusal): 'N lines still await written approval', 'N released before every signature: ratification owed', 'N items released to a person with no signed receipt', 'N donated lines unreceipted', 'N signed approvals not filed', each read off the existing one-rule functions.
findings.vnote: By code. closeOpenWorkFlag (24595-24611) names rooms not cleared, leaving lines with no recipient, and lines out with an appraiser. The close confirm (24644-24656) adds only the midpoint and ledgerCloseFlag. Nothing names _invAwaitingApproval, invRatificationOwed, invReceiptOwed, unreceipted donations or unfiled approvals, though the Releases bar computes each (v2: '1 signed receipt owed · 1 on the request still unsigned'). The proposal is a flag, never a refusal, which fits the rules.
findings.vrepro: havellin.html:24595-24656; EST-verify/out/v2.out (bar bits)

findings.title: On a values tier the Disposition Ledger carries no carrying value or gain/loss, which is what an accounting needs
findings.where: printDispositionLedger / dispositionLedger (havellin.html:34374, 34445): columns Item #, Item, Disposition, Channel / recipient, Authorized by, Date, Gross, Fees, Net, Receipt.
findings.evidence: EST/e12.js: ledger tail reads 'This ledger records where each item went and what it brought; it does not state what anything is worth.' The Trust Schedule (e7) says it 'contains no receipts or disbursements, no gains or losses on sale … all of which a §736.08135 accounting requires'.
findings.tc_impact: The trust officer or PR builds the accounting by hand from two papers: the schedule's date-of-death values against the ledger's proceeds, and in-kind distributions at value. That is exactly the spreadsheet work Havellin means to replace.
findings.proposal: Where the tier states values (docTierProduces values) and the matter is an estate, add 'Inventory value (date of death)' and, on sold lines, 'Gain / (loss)' columns with totals, plus the value of each distribution in kind and donation. Keep today's ledger on the contents and none tiers. Counsel to confirm the wording.
findings.decided_conflict: Domain rule (P19, Client documents): the Disposition Ledger is 'a record of Havellin's own work, never a valuation (INV_CONTRACT_DOCS)'. Proposed only on tiers where Havellin already states the values.
findings.vnote: The description is accurate: the ledger's columns carry no value, and its foot reads 'it does not state what anything is worth' (34554). The P19 stance in code (17630: the ledger is 'a record of Havellin's own work, never a valuation') and the Domain rule that the Trust Schedule 'supports an accounting and is not one' mean gain/loss columns move Havellin toward accounting work it deliberately leaves to counsel and the accountant. Nothing on the Decided list forbids it, but it is Anthony's and counsel's call, and the values are already on the schedules by item number, so I rate it low.

findings.title: Fiduciaries approve a sale with no price: there is no offer or reserve on a selling line
findings.where: Release Approval Request rows for Sell / Auction / Consign (printApprovalRequest 32310); the line record has gross and fees only (no reserve or offer field; grep finds none).
findings.evidence: EST/e1.js: '10 Walnut dresser … $450 Sell Palm Beach Estate Buyers' is the whole approval. The estimated value is the only figure, and nothing records what the buyer offered or the auction's reserve.
findings.tc_impact: A trust officer approves sales on price. Without it they phone or email the TC, adding a round, or they approve blind, which counsel will question when the gross comes in at $90.
findings.proposal: An optional 'Offer / reserve' field on selling lines, typed by the TC or proposed by Agent Two from comparables. The request prints 'Sell to Palm Beach Estate Buyers for $400 (offer)' or 'Auction at Kodner, reserve $1,800', and the ledger flags a gross below it. Treat the field as part of EST-01's pinned approval.
findings.vnote: grep finds no reserve, offer or asking-price field on a line. The request row for a sale is only the estimated value plus the disposition and the buyer (v1: '10 Walnut dresser … $450 Sell Palm Beach Estate Buyers'). Whether trust officers expect sale terms on the release is an expert judgement I cannot test here, but it is sound for a buyout to an estate buyer. Nothing decided conflicts.
findings.vrepro: grep -n -i 'reserve\b|offerAmt|askingPrice' havellin.html (no field); EST-verify/out/v1-request.html

findings.title: Junk lines on an estate need written approval but have no sign-out, so nothing records the hauler taking them
findings.where: signoutLineKind (havellin.html:31623) returns '' for Junk; INV_RELEASE_DISPOSITIONS (31217) includes Junk; the ledger's Date reads dispDate only (KNOWN: the Date column; the new impact is that Junk has no route to a gone record).
findings.evidence: Code: pickup covers INV_SALE_DISPOSITIONS, donation covers Donate, receipt covers Distribute; Junk falls through. The desk guide's sign-out section lists selling vendors, charities, appraisers and persons only.
findings.tc_impact: On a full house the junk load is often the largest group. It needs both fiduciaries' approval, then leaves with no signature, no gone mark and a ledger line dated '—'.
findings.proposal: A 'removal' sign-out kind for a hauler (one sheet per load: the hauler signs on the glass, lines marked gone, custody 'Released · Removal'), with SIGNED_RECORD_KINDS and signoutGroups extended. It reads 'Disposed of' on family papers.
findings.vnote: Confirmed with a correction. signoutLineKind (31623-31628) returns '' for Junk: pickup covers INV_SALE_DISPOSITIONS only, donation covers Donate and receipt covers Distribute. Junk is in INV_RELEASE_DISPOSITIONS (31217), so an estate needs written approval for it. The claim that nothing records the hauler taking the load overstates it: the record's 'Date of Disposition' (dispDate, INV_COLS 28439) marks a line gone (invRecordedGone 31926). That route is per line, with no bulk-bar field and no signature. It overlaps the KNOWN item that the ledger's Date column reads only dispDate; the new impact is that the largest group on a full house has no sign-out route.
findings.vrepro: havellin.html:31217, 31623-31628, 31924-31936, 28439; bulk bar menus 40147-40162 (no dispDate)

findings.title: The approver can be someone with no fiduciary standing, and a corporate trustee has no signing officer
findings.where: EXECUTOR_ROLES (havellin.html:10621) offers Estate Attorney, Family Member and Executor for the authorized representative; jobFiduciaries (no role filter) feeds the request's 'Approved by … / authorized fiduciary' lines and invApprovalComplete.
findings.evidence: Code: a representative recorded as 'Family Member' or 'Estate Attorney' is addressed and signs as 'authorized fiduciary', and their signature completes releases. A bank trustee ('Northern Trust, N.A.') would sign as 'Northern Trust, N.A., Trustee / authorized fiduciary', with no field for the officer who signs or their title.
findings.tc_impact: The release authority on the paper may not be the person the Letters or the Certification name. A bank trust officer expects 'Trustee, by its authorized officer, Name, Title'.
findings.proposal: On an estate, flag in amber on the Releases card and Edit Client a representative whose role is not a fiduciary role for the matter (Family Member or Estate Attorney on the probate or trust track). Add an optional 'Signing officer and title' for a corporate fiduciary, printed on the request, schedules and ledger as '<Trustee>, by <officer>, <title>' and matched by samePerson for approvals.
findings.vnote: EXECUTOR_ROLES (10621-10631) offers Estate Attorney, Executor, Family Member, Personal Representative, Trustee, court roles and Other for the representative. jobFiduciaries (7155) has no role filter. The request and schedules print '<name>, <role> / authorized fiduciary' (32548, 34187). There is no field for a corporate trustee's signing officer and title. On the probate track activation needs the Letters, so a 'Family Member' label there is mostly cosmetic; the bank-trustee officer gap is the real one for Palm Beach. That is an expert judgement, not driven. No decided rule conflicts: POA was removed for a different reason.

findings.title: To get a 40-line, two-fiduciary approval done in one round: the planned DocuSign route needs per-line approve/strike and group initials
findings.where: Releases card Send request / Record the signed request (CLAUDE.md Open work: 'a DocuSign route for the request on an estate … still to build').
findings.evidence: EST/e2.js: today one round is 11 TC presses plus, for each fiduciary, print, initial each group and own box, sign, scan and reply. Any struck line (EST-05) or changed line (EST-01) means another full round, and same-day separate returns are two recordings (EST-12).
findings.tc_impact: Days per round for the family or trust officer, and per-signer typing and ticking for the TC.
findings.proposal: Build the DocuSign envelope from printApprovalRequest's own rows: both fiduciaries in parallel at routing order 1, an initial tab on each group row, own-initial and firearms tabs, and a per-line 'approve / strike' checkbox with an optional note. On completed, record each signer's approvals per line with authFor (EST-01), record strikes as declines (EST-05), file the completed PDF and certificate through esignArchiveSigned/fileSignedCopy, and stamp the request as signed. The iPad route (P28 pad) is for a fiduciary present in the house.
findings.vnote: CLAUDE.md Open work, 'Next, decided 2026-10-26': 'still to build: a DocuSign route for the request on an estate ("Yes, build it next"; "definitely docusign"): each fiduciary initials each group and signs, and completion records the approvals and files the signed copy.' The per-line approve/strike checkbox is a useful addition to that item, and it is what would close EST-05 and the post-send half of EST-01 in the same build. Today's 11-press round is consistent with v2's flow.
findings.vrepro: CLAUDE.md Open work ('Next, decided 2026-10-26'); EST-verify/out/v2.out

findings.title: The Trust Schedule is offered and prints 'Held in Trust' on probate-only, contested and unanswered desks; the Court Inventory on an unanswered Estate Settlement prints as a §733.604 filing
findings.where: More ▾ (same menu on every matter); printTrustSchedule and printCourtInventory.
findings.evidence: EST/e7.js: unanswered, neither and contested probate all offer 'Court Inventory' and 'Trust Schedule'. Contested: 'Schedule of Tangible Personal Property Held in Trust … this estate has no trust in it'. Unanswered Estate Settlement: the Court Inventory says 'reported separately in the personal representative's §733.604 filing' while the package and route treat the matter as off probate. KNOWN sibling: the Court Inventory offered on a trust-only desk is already listed.
findings.tc_impact: A wrong instrument is one tap from being handed over, and the menu does not reflect what the matter needs.
findings.proposal: More ▾ offers the Court Inventory only where jobOnProbateTrack, the Trust Schedule only where matterDef(job).trust. On an unanswered matter, offer both with 'matter type not recorded: set it in Edit Client'.
findings.vnote: KNOWN: Open work (core-jobs run) says 'the Court Inventory is still offered on a trust-only desk under More ▾ (it refuses on its face, by design)'. The Trust Schedule on a no-trust matter is the mirror case and is just as deliberate. More ▾ gates on the tier only (39432, 39439), and printTrustSchedule stamps DRAFT 'this estate has no trust in it' (34262). The one new piece is small: an Estate Settlement with no matter recorded prints the Court Inventory as a §733.604 filing, while the desk's Urgent strip already flags the unanswered matter in amber.
findings.vrepro: havellin.html:39432, 39439, 34237-34265; CLAUDE.md Open work (core-jobs run)

findings.title: Close-out ledger card says 'the client signs' on an estate
findings.where: Disposition Ledger card heading (havellin.html:34688): '(the close-out summary the client signs)'; the line below reads 'the Personal Representative signs it at close-out'.
findings.evidence: EST/e12.js CLOSING text: 'Disposition Ledger (the close-out summary the client signs) … No signed copy on file — the Personal Representative signs it at close-out.'
findings.tc_impact: On a decedent's job 'the client' is the deceased; the card contradicts itself.

findings.vnote: On Ashworth the card reads 'Disposition Ledger (the close-out summary the client signs)' (34688), while the code's own line below says 'the <approver> signs it at close-out'.
